_frame_inset_note: REFERENCE PX KEPT CLEAR OF THE FRAME AT EVERY CUTOUT EDGE THIS SCREEN PUTS TEXT AGAINST, and it is measured rather than chosen. Until 4 September 2026 the labels started at the cutout's own left edge and every one of them was drawn partly under the frame's metal rim - RESERVE, INCOME, FREIGHTERS, FOOD and RESEARCH all losing part of their first letter, and the right-aligned VALUES losing their last pixels to the same rim at the other end. It read as a resolution-dependent glitch, clear at 1926x1079 and clipped at 1931x1076, and it was not: the overlap is there at EVERY size including 1920x1080, and what changes with the window is the font size meeting it - 18 px keeps the stem, 16 px does not. TWO THINGS PUT TEXT UNDER THE FRAME: frame_holes.to_ref adds BLEED = 2 reference px OUTWARD on each side so panel FILLS cover the anti-aliased rim, which is right for a fill and wrong for a glyph, and the artwork's rim reaches a little further in on top of that. MEASURED at the six label rows across eight window sizes from 1280x720 to 3840x2160: the opaque frame reaches at most 4.50 reference px past the box's left edge and 3.01 past its right. 8 covers the worst of those with room for the smoothscaled rim at a size nobody tested. NOT MEASURED AT THE CORNERS, deliberately - the rounded corners are opaque far into the box and a max() over every row reports 388 px; the number that matters is the one at the rows text is drawn on. This does NOT make decision 44 worse, it makes it honest: 286 was never the column a reader could see, some 7 or 8 of it was always under metal, so the drawn width was about 278 and was being reported as 286. See colonyempire.value_column and list._frame_bleed_note, which is the same observation about list_area, where pad_x 22 already covered it. SECOND FINDING, 4 September 2026, and it is why this key sits at the top level rather than inside `empire`: the colony NAME is right-aligned and its overflow is allowed to grow LEFT into list.pad_x (see list._name_gap_note), and the bound was list_area's own left edge - so a maximally long name ran under the rim exactly as the sidebar labels did. One pixel of a ten-W name at 1600x900, found by the tree-wide Class A check and by nothing else. Two blocks now need the same number and two copies of a number that must agree is this project's oldest fault, so there is ONE key and both read it. NOT a shared helper: that is the second copy of the RULE, and the third is the signal to extract (fundament, 'The third copy is the signal to extract').

empire._colour_note: CORRECTED 2 September 2026, and the correction matters. This note first said the two per-line prefixes were COLOUR attributes, label and value. In orion2re 1.60 they are NOT. ESTRINGS::s_0_0055110c and s_1_00551110 (estrings.cpp:8-9) are the C literals "\0320" and "\0321", and those compile to the bytes 1A 30 and 1A 31 - octal 032 is 0x1A, not ESC. FMTPARA dispatches 0x1A to Set_Justification_ and 0x1B to Set_Current_Colors_ (fmtpara.cpp:364-368), so the two prefixes are JUSTIFICATION codes. Only the red one is a colour: ERIC::Red_If_Negative_Fmt_String_ (eric.cpp:176) returns "\0332" = bytes 1B 32 = Set_Current_Colors_('2'), which sets color_attr = code << 5 (fmtpara.cpp:1154). THE PART THAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED: red-if-negative is the original's and applies to Income ALONE - Food is signed but never turns red, however negative it gets, and warn_negative on any other row is an HD EXTENSION (see _warn_negative_note). THE PART THAT DID NOT: there is no per-line label colour and no per-line value colour in 1.60. A 1.31 archive was cited as having \0330 and \0331, which WOULD be ESC and WOULD be colours; that has not been checked against a 1.31 tree and is exactly the kind of difference this version tag exists to expose.
empire._red_note: CHECKED AND KEPT, after a query that it might rest on a mis-transcribed byte. It does not. ERIC::Red_If_Negative_Fmt_String_ (eric.cpp:176) returns the literal "\0332", and a C octal escape is greedy to three digits: \033 is 0x1B (ESC), leaving '2' as a plain character, so the bytes are 1B 32 and FMTPARA routes 0x1B to Set_Current_Colors_ (fmtpara.cpp:364-368, :1154). Three things agree: the bytes, the function's own comment ('ESC + 2 emits a text-attribute control sequence'), and colsum.cpp itself, which spells the same effect "\x1B" "2" at :567, :575 and :1189. Contrast the JUSTIFICATION pair, where "\0320" takes \032 = 0x1A - same-looking literal, one octal digit apart, opposite meaning. That is the trap, and it is on the other pair. What IS open about these symbols is an array size, not a value: see _open_note.
empire._warn_negative_note: HD EXTENSION on two of the three rows that carry it. The original turns exactly one line red, Income, via Red_If_Negative_Fmt_String_ on surplus_bc (eric.cpp:176) - Food is printed with an explicit sign but in the value colour however negative it is, and Freighters has neither sign nor colour. This screen colours all three, because a negative food or freighter balance is the same class of fact as a negative income and the original's restraint there is a 16-colour-palette economy rather than a judgement. Income is TRANSCRIBED; food and freighters are the extension.
empire._open_note: TWO OPEN ITEMS, both read in orion2re 1.60. (1) THE ATTRIBUTE SYMBOLS ARE DECLARED AT TWO SIZES AND DEFINED THREE TIMES. colsum.h:87-88 and strings.h:39-40 declare s_0_0055110c and s_1_00551110 as const char[3]; estrings.h:9-10 declares the same names const char[4]. There are three definitions in three namespaces - COLSUM (colsum.cpp:36-37, [3], octal), ESTRINGS (estrings.cpp:8-9, [4], octal) and strings (strings.cpp:22,24, [3], hex). All three produce the same bytes, so nothing misbehaves today, and the VALUE is not in doubt. The declaration disagreement is, and it is a question for Joes rather than a fix request: see doc/orion2re_open_fixes.md. (2) E_Strings_(12) has no entry in orion2_str.h - no name, no comment - so its text is unknown and only its USES can be read. Every use in the tree is consistent with the empty string: button and hotkey labels where the sprite carries the artwork (colsum.cpp:263-302, colbldg.cpp:346-364), 'no help text' (colsysdi.cpp:212), 'no prefix' (colsum.cpp:563 when a star is not blockaded), and the not-negative branch of Red_If_Negative_Fmt_String_ (eric.cpp:178). Consistent is not confirmed. Nothing here depends on it; the 'Buy' label in list._buy_note is a word this project chose precisely because 12 could not supply one.
empire._join_note: Read in orion2re 1.60. The six are built into ONE buffer and printed once. ERIC::String_Builder2_ (eric.cpp:425) formats each line, then for build_mode != 0 joins it to what is already there with snprintf(dest, size, E_Strings_(71), existing, 13, new) - E_Strings_(71) is '%s%c%s' and the character is the literal 13. So the separator is a CARRIAGE RETURN, not a newline, and the whole block reaches FMTPARA::Print_Formatted_Paragraph_ as a single string.
empire._justify_note: SETTLED, and it reverses what this note said twice before. THE LAYOUT: each entry is ONE row, label LEFT and value RIGHT. The two per-line prefixes are justification codes - s_0_0055110c is the bytes 1A 30 = Set_Justification_('0') and s_1_00551110 is 1A 31 = Set_Justification_('1'), and FMTPARA routes 0x1A to Set_Justification_ (fmtpara.cpp:364-368). Justify_Line_ (fmtpara.cpp:1699) implements mode 1 by adding the whole remaining width to the first character's advance, which is right alignment; the right edge is para.x2 = x + width - 1 = 623 of 640 (fmtpara.cpp:657). ONE ROW AND NOT TWO: Set_Justification_ (fmtpara.cpp:999) flushes the pending segment through Complete_Line_ when char_count > 0 but never advances y - y moves only on CR, LF, VT and FF (fmtpara.cpp:322-341, where CR falls through to Vertical_Move_Line_Advance_). The CR that String_Builder2_ joins the six with is what ends each row. WHY justify=3 IS INERT, corrected: not because CR terminates each line, though it would also do that. The buffer BEGINS with s_0, so the very first thing the parser meets is Set_Justification_('0') with char_count still 0 - it skips the flush entirely and assigns justify_mode = 0 (fmtpara.cpp:1017). Mode 3 is overwritten before a single character is drawn and never reaches Justify_Line_. WHY THIS WAS WRONG TWICE: an octal 032 read as 033. '\0320' looks like ESC + '0' and is SUB + '0' - a C octal escape is greedy to three digits, so \032 = 0x1A, not \033 = 0x1B. Read as ESC it is a colour code and the six lines are plain left-aligned text; read correctly it is a justification code and the original does label-left/value-right. The 1.60 tree settles it three ways: two files spell the pair '\0320'/'\0321' (colsum.cpp:36-37, estrings.cpp:8-9) and a third spells it '\x1A' '0' / '\x1A' '1' (strings.cpp:22, :24) - unambiguous, and commented in the source itself as 'switches paragraph justification to left alignment' and 'to right alignment'. THE INVENTION IS NOW THE OTHER WAY ROUND: label-left/value-right is the TRANSCRIPTION and is what this screen draws; the stacked, centred label-over-value it drew until 2 September 2026 was the invention.

empire._native_width_note: DEVIATION, live at every resolution. The width of the original's empire paragraph in its own 640x480 pixels: Print_Formatted_Paragraph_(520, 354, 104, buffer, 3) at colsum.cpp:418, read in orion2re 1.60. The right edge of a VALUE is x + width - 1 = 623 (para.x2, fmtpara.cpp:657), and THAT alignment is transcribed. The WIDTH is not: 104 scaled by REF_W / 640 is 312 reference px against the 286 the sidebar cutout gives, so screen.py clamps to the cutout and the clamp fires everywhere. 286 against 312 is 8.3 % of the column - every value sits 26 reference px left of the original's proportion. The star name under it is Draw_Scan_Info_'s, centred at native (444, 431) (colsum.cpp:86), and it names the SELECTED colony's star, which is the selection this screen already holds. inset._deviation_note: THREE DEVIATIONS, all forced and all marked in colonyinset.py. (1) THE SPRITE IS DRAWN, NOT BLITTED. view_mode 3 blits MOX::_colony_galaxy_star_seg[color_idx] (movebox.cpp:99-102), gstar.lbx entries 23..32 (colony.cpp:329-338) - the player's own LBX, which this project does not redistribute, the same wall list._buy_note and the morale sprites hit. The SHAPE is not invented: it was read off the original's framebuffer and is a 3x3 plus, dark arms and a bright centre, with the black hole a 3x3 ring around a near-black core - which is also why the original's draw call offsets by (-1, -1). (2) THE COLOURS ARE THE SKIN'S, NOT THE GAME'S PALETTE. The eight owner colours come from galaxy_map.renderer.OWNER_COLORS, which is the one home for them; a second hardcoded table read off one savegame is the name-table failure this project has paid for twice. Each colour is a hand-picked palette PAIR in the original (measured ratios 0.5 to 0.78) and here it is one bright colour dimmed by a single factor. Colours 3, 4 and 5 were never measured at all - no player in the reference save carries them. (3) THE MAP DOES NOT FILL THE HOLE. See _geometry_note.
inset._geometry_note: THE BOX IS 253 x 200 REFERENCE PX AND THE MAP FILLS IT, decided 6 September 2026 - doc/colony_inset_geometry.md Part 3, and screens/colony_summary/layout_reference.json is where the rectangle is typed. THE CROP IS THE ORIGINAL'S COVERAGE AND NOT THE GALAXY: the original's box reaches 50.6*M x 40*M world units (movebox.cpp:20-21 with M = _max_map_scale; the 50.6 here is 506/10, the map viewport's own width per scale unit, and NOT the retired MAP_MAX_X/scale estimate that carried the same digits - see core/zoomtables.GALAXY_VIEWPORT_W), whose aspect is 1.2651 at EVERY galaxy size because both divisors are constants and M cancels. 253/200 = 1.2650 against that, so the crop fills the box with NO LETTERBOX AT ANY SIZE, including orion2re's Maximum - the earlier expectation that Maximum letterboxes is WITHDRAWN, and it only held if the crop were the galaxy (1800 x 1350, aspect 1.3333) rather than the original's reach. The scale is exactly 5/M reference px per world unit; at 3840x2160 the box is 506 x 400 device px, the small galaxy's own world extent at 1:1. HD EXTENSION - THE INSET'S SCALE IS FIXED AND OFF THE RUNG LADDER. Expressed as a map_scale the inset sits at 2M: 20, 30, 40, 60, 72 for the five sizes, and three of the five are not values zoomtables.scale_rungs can stand on. The marking's reason is NOT 'between rungs' though - the inset does not zoom at all, so it never stands on a rung, and the two sizes that land on one do so by arithmetic coincidence. Milder than hd_zoom_level, which interpolates a ladder the original does stand on. DEVIATION - ISOTROPIC WHERE THE ORIGINAL IS NOT. The original compresses y by a constant 3953/4395 = 0.89943 (movebox.cpp:20-21), so an isotropic HD inset is NOT the original's picture scaled: it is the original's COVERAGE re-projected without the squash, and every constellation in it is 11.2 % taller relative to its width. Chosen because a galaxy is a shape. THE EARLIER READING THAT STOOD HERE IS WITHDRAWN: it scaled the original's own 128 x 91 picture uniformly, which keeps the squash, and in the same box the two differ by 11 % of content width from the same data. The numbers are in doc/colony_inset_geometry.md 3.5 and are deliberately not repeated here - two readings of one inset in one tree is what this note used to be. NOT FIXED BY WIDENING THE HOLE: deriving artwork from a deviation to make the deviation go away is decision 44's second half. STILL STANDING: boxes.json's galaxy_inset is the old 451 x 203 and colonyinset still draws into it; that is the rebuild's Stage 4 and is a debt, not a second reading.
inset._not_drawn_note: THREE THINGS THE ORIGINAL DOES HERE AND THIS DOES NOT, recorded rather than left to be noticed. THE SCANNED STAR ANIMATES: view_mode 3 resets every star's animation frame except the scanned one (movebox.cpp:98-101), so that one star cycles. Reachable - the selection is known - and not drawn because the frames are in the unshipped LBX. THE STARS ARE FIELDS: _galaxy_map_star_field[] (colsum.cpp:69-75), and hovering one in the original sets the scanned star AND moves _g_colony_n to the best colony there; this inset is display only. THE CONNECT LINE: Colsum_Connect_Galaxy_Map_Stars_ (colsum.cpp:731) draws an animated multi-coloured line between two stars, and its caller (colsum.cpp:487-498) fires ONLY while COLMOVE::_cluster_colony_n != -1 - a population transfer being dragged between colonies. OrionLayer has no colonist dragging, so there is no state in which that line would be drawn. Written down because 'Connect' reads like a permanent feature of the map and is not one.

WHICH HOLE IS WHICH IS DERIVED FROM THE SOURCE, not from left-to-right position - until 4 September 2026 frame_holes.py assigned these three names by index and had the last two the wrong way round. galaxy_inset is the RIGHTMOST of the three and is the original's own map hole: MOVEBOX::Draw_Galaxy_Map_Box_(nullptr, 0, 0x17c, 0x15d, 0x80, 0x5b, ...) at colsum.cpp:415 draws the small galaxy map at native (380, 349, 128, 91) (movebox.cpp:4-9), which is reference (1140, 785, 384, 205), centre x 1332. spare_panel is the MIDDLE one, over native x ~193-347, where the original draws its production and morale sprite column (Draw_Colony_Wee_Prod_(..., 106, y_pos, 366, 20), colsum.cpp:1171-1176) - values output_panel already answers for, which is what makes that hole the spare rather than a second place to draw the same thing. A smoke check asserts the rule (nearest hole to the native rect must be the one named galaxy_inset, and decisively nearest) rather than the list, so a re-generated frame cannot quietly reassign the names again. ONE PANEL PER STEP - spare_panel is empty on purpose and not waiting on anything in this file. The names are the plate's own windows now, from layout_reference.json through frame_holes.py, so this list and the artwork cannot drift. REVERSED 12 September 2026, and the fill follows the hole: the one sort_bar is seven boxes again, sort_name / sort_population / sort_food / sort_industry / sort_science / sort_producing / sort_bc, because Data's artwork cuts a slot per key. Every one of them is listed here for the same reason the other six are - a cutout that shows content gets the panel fill, and a sort slot shows a word. It was never listed while it was one bar: the strip drew its own background through colonysort.render and the hole sat over the raw background between the lit boxes, which is a difference nobody would see until a slot is narrow enough to frame what is behind it. panels._galaxy_inset_fill_note: BLACK, and it is a measurement rather than a taste. The panel fill this screen lays down is PANEL_BG (8, 11, 20); the ORIGINAL's own inset region measures (0, 8, 0) over 2475 of about 2700 samples in the 640x480 frame at native (380, 349, 128, 91). So the box already had a fill - the cockpit texture was never showing through - and black moves TOWARD the original rather than away from it. It is a per-box fill and not a change to colonyinset, which deliberately draws no background of its own: Draw_Galaxy_Map_Box_ fills black only when _using_colony_screen_palette == 0 (movebox.cpp:36-38) and this screen sets that flag, so the original inherits whatever the screen put there and so do we.

list._invention: INVENTION. The original draws three columns of population sprites per row, one icon per colonist, squished when a colony outgrows its column (COLDRAW::Do_Colony_Info_Pop_Stuff_For_Pop_, coldraw.cpp:282; Calculate_Squish_Step_, coldraw.cpp:12). This draws one allocation bar per row instead: one square per colonist, three zones in ECON order. MOO2 could not draw it and does not. Marked here, in colonylist.py (the renderer), in v3_projektstatus.md and in a smoke check. WHAT THE ORIGINAL'S SPRITES ACTUALLY ARE, measured 4 September 2026 off the game's own framebuffer because RACEICON.LBX is the player's file and is not shipped. COLONY::People_Anim_ (colony_main.cpp:444) loads entry race_idx * 13 + job_type * 2 (+1 for pop_state 2), so they are RACE-SPECIFIC figures and not generic profession icons; natives are entry 0xAA and androids 0xA9, one each for every race. Drawn in a 30x31 native cell at 30 px spacing, squished by Calculate_Squish_Step_ when the column is crowded. In the reference save's race the three read as: farmer bronze with a tall hoe, worker teal with a hammer, scientist white/silver with a cyan-and-red instrument - distinct by COLOUR first and by the tool's silhouette second. Scaled to our slot they stay tellable apart from about 1920x1080 up (tile 20x30, 67 % of the sprite's width); at 1280x720 (13x20, 43 %) the colour survives and the tool does not. ONLY ONE RACE WAS SEEN - another race's set may separate less well, and nothing here has checked that. TWO THINGS THE COMPARISON IS NOT: the sprite at its own proportion does NOT fit this track, because 42 slots of 30 px need 1342 reference px against the 922 the budget has (see _horizontal_budget), so icons here would be squeezed to about two thirds width whatever else is decided; and the original's own detail is LEAST available when it matters most - at twelve farmers the figures overlap into a picket fence with only the last one fully visible, while these squares never overlap at all.
list._figure_anchor_deviation: DEVIATION - THE VERTICAL ANCHOR, TOP -> BOTTOM. Data's decision of 12 September 2026. The original hangs a row's population sprites from the TOP of the row: the icon row is 31*i + 38 (COLSUM::Draw_Info_Pop_For_, colsum.cpp:685, mode 0 of COLDRAW::Do_Colony_Info_Pop_Stuff_For_Pop_, which draws at top_y) and the field it sits in runs 31*i + 35 to 31*i + 65 INCLUSIVE (colsum.cpp:283-291; a field's y_end is its last row, fields.cpp:708 and :1268). That is a 31-row band around a 28-row canvas: 3 px above the sprite and ZERO below it - the canvas's last row IS the band's last row, confirmed on the original's own framebuffer (evidence/colony_summary_native_split.png: row 0 top line at native 35, ink 38..61, plate border 62-63, next row's top line at 66, against an Elerian farmer master that inks rows 0..23 of 28). HD's band is list_area divided by ten and is whatever the window makes it - 58 px at 1920x1080 against a 56 px sprite, but 73 at 3440x1371 and 77 at 2560x1440. Transcribing the TOP anchor put all of that slack UNDER the figures, and a row's colonists floated over their own row: 17 px of empty band at 3440x1371, 21 at 2560x1440, and only 2 at 1080p, which is why it was invisible where it was checked. So the sprite is anchored to the band's FLOOR instead and the slack goes above - and what is put on the floor is the INK, not the canvas. ANCHORING THE CANVAS WAS THE FIRST ATTEMPT, ON 12 September 2026, AND IT STILL FLOATED AT EVERY SIZE: a master inks to row 23 of its 28 (51 of the 54) or to row 24 (the three Bulrathi), so a canvas on the floor hangs its sprite 4 master rows up - 8 device px at step 2, 16 at step 4, and the transparent tail is what floats. The rule is origin_y = plate_inner_floor - ink_bottom, where plate_inner_floor is the row above the cell plate's bottom border (band_bottom - 1 - PLATE_LINE) and ink_bottom is THAT sprite's own last inked row, measured on the stepped surface at load (colonyfigures.FigureSet.ink_bottom). AT NATIVE SCALE THE ORIGINAL DOES THE SAME THING and the two anchors agree: its ink ends at native 61, the row above its plate's border at 62-63, and the four rows of tail are spent on that border and the two rows under it, so a step of 1 reproduces it exactly. The original never steps, so it never has to answer for a tail 8 or 16 px deep - that is where this parts from it, and it is one deviation with the edge, not two. The cost is that the three Bulrathi sprites, whose ink is one row taller, come up one row against their neighbours where the original leaves them one row lower. The held cluster reads the same function (colonytrack.figure_origin_y through held_figure_y), so a figure in hand and a figure in a row cannot land on different lines. It ENDS if the bands ever become the original's own 31 rows per step. Marked in colonytrack.figure_origin_y, in colonylist where the blit is, here, in v3_projektstatus.md and in a smoke check.

list._hd_extension_popup: HD EXTENSION. HOVERING A JOB GROUP SHOWS A POPUP BELOW THE ROW. The original has no hover text on this screen at all: it answers a hover by SCANNING - Evaluate_Colony_Pop_Input_ assigns COLONY::_g_colony_n from the scanned field (colsum.cpp:880-890) and the bottom-left box redraws for that colony - so the information exists there and appears somewhere else entirely. In colonypopup, here, in v3_projektstatus.md and in a check.
list._cell_marks_note: HD EXTENSION. AN IDENTITY LETTER IN THE CELL, and the fill is not touched. The original draws a pop as race * 13 + job * 2 + 1 (colony_main.cpp:445), profession and race in one figure, except for three classes that get one sprite each: a native is entry 0xAA whatever it does, an android 0xA9, a conquered pop a static race portrait (colony.cpp:1278). The profession there is carried by WHICH COLUMN the sprite stands in; the HD row has one track and no columns, so the cell carries both - fill for the profession, letter for the identity. The player's own pops carry NO letter, because that is over ninety per cent of cells and they have to stay quiet. VERIFICATION IS SPLIT: N for a native is confirmed against fixture_natives_3502.5.GAM by three independent sources (the data, the original's picture, the label the game prints); A and C rest on the source alone, because no save this project holds contains an android or a conquered pop. A FIFTH CLASS IS DELIBERATELY UNMARKED and it is a known gap - an assimilated pop of another race (conquered bit clear, nibble not the owner's, invasion.cpp:672-676) draws like one of the player's own here while the original draws it with its own race's figure. Its natural mark is a race initial, which collides with the marker alphabet, and no fixture holds the case to judge that on.
list._overflow_note: THE LIST DROPS ROWS THAT DO NOT FIT, and until 3 September 2026 it did so in silence. render() stops at the first row that would cross the bottom of list_area; at 1920x1080 the panel holds NINE rows, and a twelve-colony empire therefore lost three with nothing on screen saying so. Every drawn row was correct and every check in the suite was green, because every check looked at rows that were drawn - the fault was found by somebody noticing a colony they owned was missing from a screenshot. The wording lives here per decision 15 and {count} is substituted by replace, not str.format (decision 37). Setting it to the empty string restores the silent behaviour, which is worth knowing and is not worth doing. THE LIST SCROLLS NOW (4 September 2026) AND THIS COUNT IS BOTH DIRECTIONS - rows above the window plus rows below it. This note used to say 'not a scrollbar and not a step towards one'; the step was taken, on its own evidence, and the sentence was rewritten rather than left to contradict the code. The wording did not have to change: '{count} more not shown' was already true of both halves. The original's own window is ten rows over the sorted list (Update_Col_List_, colsum.cpp:348) and it resets _first on every sort click (colsum.cpp:832); HD's visible count is derived from list_area and row_height and is ten only by arithmetic - see _row_height_note and fundament 46. What this line does is turn a silence into a state, the same rule the dimmed Producing header follows.

It used to be drawn below the bar at the left edge of the first job marker, which was a placement decision this file argued for on horizontal budget; the source settles it instead. COLDRAW::Do_Colony_Info_Pop_Stuff_For_Pop_ prints it in mode 0 when max_farms == 0, for the food column only: Set_Colony_Font_To_(3) then Squeeze_Print_Paragraph_(left_x, top_y + 5, right_x - left_x, 28, E_Strings_(387), 2) (coldraw.cpp:315-321). list._detail_note: The second line under the colony name; see _hd_extension for why it is marked. list._climates_note: Indexed by s_colony.climate (offset 226), the PLANET_CLIMATE enum at orion2_consts.h:362-374. THE COLONY'S FIELD, NOT THE PLANET'S, and that is source-backed rather than reasoned: Draw_Colony_Scan_Info_ takes climate_idx = colony->climate (colsum.cpp:1167) and indexes the same table. The wording is here rather than in code so a translation replaces it without touching a renderer (decision 15). Order is load-bearing: it is the enum, not an alphabetical or quality ranking.
list._hd_extension_wheel: HD EXTENSION. THE MOUSE WHEEL SCROLLS THE LIST, one row per notch over list_area. MOO2 has no wheel on this screen at all: the original moves its ten-slot window with two step buttons either side of a proportional slider - _x_fields[1] and _x_fields[2] (colsum.cpp:790-800), the bar itself drawn by Draw_Bar_Indicator_ (colsum.cpp:747-753) at native x 621..626 with its ends at 271*_first/n and 271*(_first+10)/n plus 40. THAT SLIDER IS NOT DRAWN by the HD screen and the omission is recorded rather than left to be noticed - colonylist.py's module docstring, in the same form as the blockade and the colony event. VIEWING ONLY: the scroll sends NOTHING to the game (fundament 46). The original's rows are SLOTS, so an injected click names a position in the GAME's window and _first decides which colony it reaches; this offset is ours and the game has never heard of it. Every colony is already in the snapshot, so scrolling needs nothing from the game - what must not happen is an injection while the two windows disagree, and a smoke check asserts that no scroll path injects anything. Marked here, in screen.handle_mousewheel, and in a smoke check that fails if either marking disappears.
list._hd_extension: HD EXTENSION. The 'detail' line under each colony name - climate and pops/max_pop - is drawn PER ROW. The original prints it for the SELECTED colony only, into the bottom-left scan box at native (13, 354, 80, 88): COLSUM::Draw_Colony_Scan_Info_ (colsum.cpp:1155) formats ESTRINGS::E_Strings_(74) and squeezes it into that rect, guarded by _g_colony_n != -1. The rows carry a name and nothing else. Showing it on every row makes comparable what the original could only show one at a time - the same family as the allocation bar, and not something MOO2 chose against but something its screen had no room for. It is also a SUBSET: the original's line carries planet size, gravity, mineral class and growth as well, and those are not drawn. Marked here, in colonylist.py, in v3_projektstatus.md and in a smoke check.
list._buy_note: TRANSCRIBED IN POSITION, DEVIATES TWICE IN FORM. The original adds one per row at native x=599 (colsum.cpp:302, _list_buy_fields[10], buy_btn_y_coords), to the right of the producing text, as a Locked_Button_Field_ or a hidden field depending on Colony_Can_Buy_Product_0_. That is transcribed. DEVIATION 1: the LABEL. E_Strings_(12) is empty, so 'Buy' is a word this project chose; it lives here per decision 15. DEVIATION 2: drawing TEXT AT ALL. The original's control is a SPRITE - _anims[i + 11] supplies the artwork, which is why its label string can be empty. A text button is a different object, not a translation of that one, and it is drawn this way because the sprite is in the player's LBX and is not shipped. Naming only the label would leave the larger deviation unmarked. can_buy on the row decides whether it is drawn; nothing sends a click yet.
list._width_condition_note: MARKED. squeeze_lines reduces the size until BOTH the height and the WIDTH fit. _Squeeze_Print_Paragraph_ loops on height alone, and fmtpara.cpp offers Get_Formatted_Paragraph_Max_Width_ beside the height function without calling it - so the question was whether the original lets an over-wide token overflow. It does not. _Print_Formatted_Paragraph_ places a character when char_x_end <= right_limit_x || line_started != 0 (fmtpara.cpp:567); line_started is 1 at line start and 0 after the first character (:540, :572), so the first character is placed unconditionally and every later one must fit. When one does not, Return_To_Last_Break_() is tried - breaks are recorded only at spaces, tabs and soft hyphens (:723, :731) - but _para_p->str-- runs whether it succeeded or not and the line ends (:583-587). A token with no break inside it is therefore BROKEN MID-TOKEN, and the paragraph never exceeds the width. Height alone is sufficient BECAUSE the width can never be exceeded. So: the GUARANTEE (no ink past the width, nothing truncated) is a TRANSCRIPTION and our width condition delivers it. The MEANS is a DEVIATION: the original character-wraps the token, we reduce the size and keep it whole. Visible, therefore marked. The reason is that the over-wide token here is a ship design name - user-typed data whose exact form is the point - and a hyphen-less mid-word break that reads as wrapping in a five-pixel face at 640x480 reads as corruption at HD.
list._frame_bleed_note: NOTED, NOT FIXED: the frame's metal edge overlaps the first three or four pixels of list_area on both sides, so the box's USABLE width is a little narrower than its width. Measured on 3 September 2026 while the preview's invariant check was comparing whole row bands: it reported 310 differing pixels between two renderings of the same colony, every one of them at x 0..3 or 1405..1407, and all of them frame artwork that legitimately differs between one y and another rather than anything to do with the list. IT IS HARMLESS TODAY. Nothing is drawn in that strip - pad_x is 22 px on each side and the row starts inside it - so the overlap costs nothing and no column is being clipped. IT IS WRITTEN DOWN BECAUSE THE BOX IS DERIVED FROM THE ARTWORK. frame_holes.py reads the transparent holes out of frame.png (decision 3), so the box is exactly the hole and the hole is exactly what the drawing left open - which means the bleed is not an error anywhere, and the next person to measure ink against the box edge will find pixels they did not put there and have to work out why. This is that answer, ahead of the question. Anything comparing rendered pixels against list_area should inset by pad_x or work in the track's own coordinates, which is what colony_list_preview.colony_track_rect does and says.
list._row_count_note: TEN, AND IT IS THE ORIGINAL'S OWN WINDOW. COLSUM::_list_col[10] holds ten slots and Update_Col_List_ fills exactly that many (colsum.cpp:348), so ten rows is what the original shows at any resolution and what this screen shows at all three. IT IS A VALUE AND NOT A BOX: a row is not a rectangle anybody places, it is the list window divided by this number - colonytrack.band_height, with the remainder going to the LAST band the way the columns and the header plates take theirs. NINE VALUES DIED WHEN IT ARRIVED, on 8 September 2026: row_height, pad_x, pad_y, name_width, name_gap, bar_height, tail_width, building_width and growth_gap. Every one of them answered a question a COLUMN BOX or this count now answers, and a tuned number that agrees with a derived one is the second copy decision 5 is about - row_height 58 and pad_y 14 happened to yield ten rows at all three resolutions, by arithmetic coincidence rather than by construction, and nothing said so.
list._columns_note: THE SIX COLUMNS ARE BOXES - col_name, col_farmers, col_workers, col_scientists, col_building, col_scroll - in boxes.json, F5-draggable like anything else (decisions 14 and 5). ONE RECT SOURCE EACH: the header plate above a column, the cells inside it and the drop target over it all read the same box, where the header used to tile its own box from a ref-width table and colonytrack tiled a second one. THE SCROLL SLOT IS A BOX TOO and that is deliberate: colonyscroll draws its arrows there and colonyheader draws a plate there, so making it 'the remainder' would have given one column two rect sources - the exact thing this round removes. ONLY x AND WIDTH ARE READ. A column is a strip of the list, so its y and height are list_area's; colonyheader.sync_columns holds the boxes to them so a vertical drag snaps back rather than being silently ignored and then saved. THEY ARE RESOLUTION-INDEPENDENT: a box rect is in reference space and core.layout scales it, so the six are the same numbers under every resolution key and a smoke check asserts that rule rather than the state - the editor saves only the resolution it is running at (core.box.save_boxes), which is how the two lists would drift.
list._deviation_note: WHAT EACH COLUMN DEVIATES FROM, AND THE TRANSCRIPTION IT IS MEASURED AGAINST. core/zoomtables.NATIVE_JOB_COLUMNS is the source: the Get_Selected_Pop_ literals (colsum.cpp:1006-1024) give left_x 101 / 236 / 378 and the drawn spans 135 : 142 : 134, with WORKERS the widest. What the original states is a RATIO and not a width - HD's columns are 2.53x their native ones by Data's Stage 1 decision, so the absolute number is ours and the proportion is the transcription. col_name and col_building carry deviations of their own with reasons already recorded in layout_reference._list_columns_note: the name column is wider than a proportional share because the HD row spends its extra width on the name, and the building column is wider than the 13.3 % the original's Squeeze_Print_Formatted_Paragraph_(0x200, y, 0x55, 0x16) requires because the surplus goes to the reservation rather than to figure spacing. The check reports EVERY column's deviation into v3_projektstatus.md and goes red only where one is unmarked.
list._building_column_note: THE WIDTH IS col_building's BOX SINCE 8 September 2026 - it was a `building_width` of 190 reference px, which the box now carries and the column table already carried at 314. What this note records is what the ORIGINAL states, which no box replaces. TRANSCRIBED FROM BILL::Squeeze_Print_Formatted_Paragraph_(0x200, y, 0x55, 0x16) at colsum.cpp:621 - x 512, width 85, max height 22, of 640. 85/640 is 13.3 %, which is 190 of 1408. WHY IT IS A RESERVATION: _Squeeze_Print_Paragraph_ (bill.cpp:147) passes width straight into get_height(width, text) and loops on max_height >= height. The text is WRAPPED into the width and the HEIGHT is what is made to fit; width never moves, and there is no truncation branch in that function at all. TWO LINES, AND THE ORIGINAL BUDGETS TWO IN THE SAME BOX: max height 0x16 = 22 goes into a row whose pitch is 31 (buy_btn_y_coords steps 35, 65, 96, 128 ...), so that box is two thirds of its row and holds more than one line of its own font. The two-line column is the same PLACE as the original's, not just the same technique used elsewhere. TRANSCRIBED BEHAVIOUR, NOT MECHANISM: wrap into the width, reduce size until it fits, never truncate. The original's first squeeze step narrows the SPACE GLYPH (font_style_widths[32]--), a bitmap-font trick with no Aldrich equivalent; its third steps between discrete bitmap faces. build_font_min is the floor, and the text is drawn whole even there - the original prints the paragraph regardless once it runs out of things to shrink. A previous pass measured this as widest string, one line, full font and got 311 px, nearly twice as much; all three of those constraints are ones the original never imposes.

move._note: OUR OWN WORDS, per decision 15, and that is not a shortcut. We refuse BEFORE injecting - the whole point of mirroring COLMOVE's rules is that a refusal can be shown as a reason instead of arriving as silence in the framebuffer - so the sentence a player reads is a thing this project chose and has to own. The original's own ESTRINGs (382 and 522) are its own, are loaded from the player's estrings.lbx at runtime, and one of the two describes a rule its code does not implement (see doc/orion2re_open_fixes.md item 8), so copying them would be wrong twice over. The RULES are transcribed in colonymove.py with their line numbers; only the wording is here.
move._count_note: EVERY LINE IS ABOUT A COUNT, NOT ABOUT A YES OR NO, and that is forced by the original rather than chosen. Send_Cluster_ walks the cluster one pop at a time and returns the moment a rule refuses (colmove.cpp:168-173), leaving the pops it already moved in their new job and the rest in hand. So a message saying 'this column will not take them' would be wrong whenever some of them fit: forty in industry and a cluster of five gives two landed and three carried. {landed} and {carried} are substituted by replace and never str.format (decision 37).
move.android: Androids keep the job they have
move.partial: only {landed} of {total} would move, {carried} would stay
move.window_fixed: The list is too short to scroll
move.past_end: That row is past the end of the list
move.sort_unavailable: This sort order cannot be matched to the game's list
move.no_icon: That square has no colonist behind it
move.other_colony: Pops can only be moved inside one colony here
move.no_pickup: The game did not pick the colonists up
move.wrong_pickup: The game picked up a different group - nothing was dropped
move.window_lost: The game's list window would not move
move.stranded: The game is holding colonists. Press RETURN to put them back.
move._stranded_note: THE ONE MESSAGE THAT ASKS THE PLAYER TO DO SOMETHING, so it names the control instead of describing it. RETURN is this screen's own button (layout.json `return`, native_click [540, 452]) and pressing it runs COLMOVE::Clear_Cluster_ (colsum.cpp:804), which is an EXACT undo: Get_Cluster_ only cleared bit 0x200 and Clear_Cluster_ sets it back, job bits untouched (colmove.cpp:39-53). So the colonists return to the jobs they had, and nothing is lost. The wording says RETURN and not `leave the screen` because both Clear_Cluster_ call sites ARE leave-the-screen paths (the other is :938, the producing field) and only one of them is a button the player can see. This state is reachable only when a send did not confirm - HD refuses every move the game would refuse before injecting - so a player who reads this sentence has already met something unexpected and should not also have to guess which control ends it.
move._partial_note: A PARTIAL MOVE IS REFUSED, AND THAT IS A DEVIATION. The original performs it: Send_Cluster_ walks the cluster one pop at a time and returns the moment Give_Colonist_New_Job_ says no (colmove.cpp:168-173), leaving the moved ones moved and the rest in hand. What every one of those four refusals ALSO does is call GENDRAW::Help_ (colmove.cpp:526, :534, :541, :555), which is TEXTBOX::Do_Text_Box_ - a BLOCKING message box, `do { ... } while (fields::Get_Input_() == 0)` (textbox.cpp:149). So a refused drop parks the game in a modal this HD screen does not draw, over a colony summary the player can no longer reach, with a cluster still held. HD therefore sends only a plan that completes, and `partial` says what WOULD have moved rather than what did. The cost is named rather than hidden: a player who wants to move two of twelve into a column with room for two cannot, where the original would let them and then show the box. It ends the day something can dismiss the box - it adds a hidden field over the whole screen (textbox.cpp:246), so one injected click would probably do it, which is a guess and is why nothing is built on it.
move._hd_extension_cancel: HD EXTENSION. RIGHT CLICK, OR A LEFT CLICK OFF THE TRACK, DISCARDS THE SELECTION. MOO2 has no cancel that stays on this screen at all: both Clear_Cluster_ call sites are leave-the-screen paths (colsum.cpp:804 and colsum.cpp:938), so in the original the only ways out of a held cluster are dropping it or leaving. The sentence this marking rests on is NOT that we are kinder - it is that the HD selection is not the game's cluster. The first click is local and injects nothing, so discarding it costs nothing and the game never hears about it. The moment a preview does inject, this extension has to go. Marked here, in colonypick.py, in colonymoveui.py, in v3_projektstatus.md and in a smoke check.
move._window_note: TWO REFUSALS THAT ARE NOT ABOUT A POP BUT ABOUT THE GAME'S LIST WINDOW, and they are here rather than in their own block because a player meets them in the same act: a move that cannot be sent because the window will not go where the row is. COLSUM::_first is the original's ten-slot offset (_list_col[10], Update_Col_List_ colsum.cpp:348-351) and an injected click names a POSITION IN THAT WINDOW, so it has to agree with the HD row first - decision 46. window_fixed: below ten colonies neither stepper runs at all (colonies_count >= num_items, colsum.cpp:210 and :226) and Update_First_ forces _first = 0 anyway (colsum.cpp:194-197), so the window cannot be moved and does not need to be. past_end: the increment is only offered while _g_colony_list_ptr[_first + 10] is a real colony (colsum.cpp:796), so _first stops at n - 10 and the last page is FULL. Both are refused rather than clamped, because a clamped target would send a click to a row nobody asked for.
move._drop_target_note: THE DROP TARGET IS THE WHOLE COLUMN CELL, AND IT IS A TRANSCRIPTION - corrected 8 September 2026, when this key said HD EXTENSION. What stood here argued that the original's three columns are fixed and always clickable while HD's zones are sized by the data, so an empty job needed a target of ours. The original's target is a FIELD and it is added unconditionally: mode 1 of COLDRAW::Do_Colony_Info_Pop_Stuff_For_Pop_ ends in fields::Add_Scroll_Field_(left_x, top_y, left_x, right_x + 8, left_x, right_x, right_x - left_x + 8, 30, ...) at coldraw.cpp:409, after a walk that may have drawn nothing - so x 101..234 / 236..376 / 378..510 at y 31*i+34..31*i+64 accept a drop whether or not the column holds an icon, and COLSUM::Evaluate_Colony_Pop_Input_ turns a hit on one into Send_Cluster_(colony, job) (colsum.cpp:869). Nothing about that is ours. THE DEVIATION IN HEIGHT IS CLOSED - 8 September 2026. It was: the original's field is 30 px of a 31 px row pitch, 97 % of the band, and ours was bar_h, 30 reference px of a 58 px row_height, 52 % - so a click in the top or bottom 14 reference px of a row discarded the selection where the original would have dropped. The row band is the list window divided by list.row_count now and the cell fills it, so the plate rect is the drop rect is the cell rect and the target is the whole band. Closed in colonytrack._column_boxes, here, in v3_projektstatus.md and in a smoke check that reads the plate's own edges off the surface. THE FOURTH TARGET IS THE COLONY NAME: _list_fields[i] with a cluster held is Send_Cluster_(_list_col[i], -1) (colsum.cpp:909), and on the colony the cluster came from that is the re-flag branch - requested_job == -1 sets 0x200 back and consults no rule (colmove.cpp:161-165), so the array ends exactly as it started. HD releases the selection and sends nothing, which reproduces that outcome without creating the game's cluster only to release it.
move._no_success_message_note: A MOVE THAT WORKED SAYS NOTHING, 9 September 2026, and the key that said it is gone. `complete` was "{landed} moved" and it was drawn into `planet_info` - which is the LEFT HALF OF THE ORIGINAL'S OWN SCAN BOX, the description paragraph at native (13, 354, 80, 88) (COLSUM::Draw_Colony_Scan_Info_, colsum.cpp:1155) - so every successful move evicted a transcription to report something the player could already see. The original marks nothing at all here: the only Fill_/Line_ calls in colsum.cpp are the scroll thumb (:759-765), no frame round a picked cell and no notice after a drop. What it does is redraw the row, and the row IS the feedback - the pops left one column and are in another and the squish changed with them. HD draws that same row from the same array. Data's two 1440p screenshots of 8 September 2026 are the pair, one with the paragraph and one with "1 moved" where it had been. A REFUSAL still speaks, and that is decision 33 rather than an exception: HD refuses before injecting so the player reads a reason, and the original's own answer to a refusal is GENDRAW::Help_, a BLOCKING text box over the whole screen (textbox.cpp:149). A transient sentence in a panel that redraws itself is the quiet version of a thing the original shouts.
move._hd_extension_notice: HD EXTENSION. `stranded` is the one line that is neither a refusal nor a result, and since 9 September 2026 it has its OWN place: a strip across the top band of the list (colonymoveui.draw_notice), never `planet_info`. A refusal may borrow that panel because it is transient and _render_info draws the paragraph back on the next frame; this notice stands until the player presses RETURN, so it would evict a transcription for an unbounded time. MOO2 shows no such strip - its answer to a held cluster is the blocking TEXTBOX::Do_Text_Box_ (textbox.cpp:149) that HD must not reproduce - which is what makes this an extension and not a transcription. The top band is the place because while the game holds a cluster the list is not actionable: every further drop compounds the mismatch, so the strip hides a row the player must not use anyway. Marked here, in colonymoveui.MoveController.__init__, in v3_projektstatus.md and in a smoke check.

words._note:
THE WORD LISTS THE SCAN BOX SUBSTITUTES, and they are OUR OWN WORDING, not the game's bytes. The original fills four tables - MOX::_planet_size_string, _mineral_class_string and _planet_gravity_string at estrings.cpp:155-169, _planet_climate_string at estrings.cpp:204-213 - and every entry is an ESTRINGS::E_Strings_(id) call, so the strings themselves come from the player's own estrings.lbx, loaded at runtime and one file per language (estrings.cpp, Load_E_Strings_). They are not in the orion2re source, they are not shipped, and nothing here extracts them - the same absence that leaves the building column empty and gave the Buy button an invented label. So these are English words this project chose to match what the game prints, and they live here rather than in a renderer so a translation replaces them without touching code (decision 15). ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: each list is indexed by its enum and is not a ranking - PLANET_SIZE at orion2_consts.h:392-397, MINERAL_RESOURCE at :328-333, PLANET_GRAVITY at :377-380. THE RULE, and it is a rule and not three separate decisions: A VALUE CARRIES NO PREFIX, BECAUSE THE LABEL CARRIES IT. This panel is a table of label-and-value pairs and the original's box is one run-on paragraph, so a word that reads correctly there reads twice here. The source draws the distinction more finely than 'our list is wrong' does. MINERALS: colland.cpp:60-62 puts the table value into its own format string, E_Strings_(0x176), and the word 'Mineral' belongs to that FORMAT - the table holds 'Rich', which is what this list holds, and 'Mineral Rich' here would render as MINERALS Mineral Rich. GRAVITY: CORRECTED 7 September 2026, when the table itself became readable. This note said colland.cpp:65 prints the table entry with no format at all, so the full string 'Normal Gravity' must be in the table. THE FIRST HALF IS RIGHT AND THE CONCLUSION IS WRONG. _planet_gravity_string holds E_Strings_(0x2AF/0x2B0/0x2B1), and the extraction gives them as 'Low G', 'Normal G', 'Heavy G' - so colland.cpp:65 really does print 'Normal G' and nothing more. The word 'Gravity' comes from the COLONY SUMMARY's own format, E_Strings_(0x4A) = '%s%s %s 
%sravity
Mineral %s
Population (%d/%d)
%s%+dk %s' (colsum.cpp:1194-1200): the slot is '%sravity' and the table supplies the 'G'. That is where the scan box's 'Normal Gravity' is assembled, and it is why reading the rendered box was not enough to know what the table held. THE LIST IS UNCHANGED and the rule above is unchanged - a label-and-value table carries the bare quality - but it now rests on the table instead of on an inference from one screen. ONE MORE THING WORTH KEEPING: 'Normal G' was rejected here as an enum name (PLANET_GRAVITY_NORMAL_G) in title case, which it looked exactly like. It is also, letter for letter, the game's own string. The rejection was right for the wrong reason, and a value that looks like an identifier artefact can still be the real one. Both lists therefore carry the bare quality and the label supplies the noun. 'Normal G' was neither: it was the enum name (PLANET_GRAVITY_NORMAL_G) in title case, which is how a list derived from identifiers rather than from the screen goes wrong. SECOND SOURCE, and it is what corrected this: the original's own scan box read 'Huge Desert / Normal Gravity / Mineral Rich / Population (4/8) / +63k' on 3 September 2026, in the first --live --native side-by-side this project ever ran. Before that the planet description for Ixion II on 31 August had confirmed 'Small Ocean, Normal Gravity, Mineral Abundant' and the direction of all three enums. CLIMATE IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. It already has a home at list.climates, with its own provenance note, and is read from there by the row renderer and by the output panel alike. A second copy that agrees today is the screen-ID-map failure waiting; a smoke check asserts the ten climate words appear in exactly one of the two blocks.

output._note: output_panel is a TRANSCRIPTION of the original's bottom-left scan box (decision 43 was withdrawn; see screen.py). Two calls fill that box for the SELECTED colony, both in COLSUM::Draw_Colony_Scan_Info_ (colsum.cpp:1155), which is guarded by _g_colony_n != -1: a formatted paragraph at native (13, 354, 80, 88) that substitutes SEVEN values into ESTRINGS::E_Strings_(74) (colsum.cpp:1196-1206), and a column of production rows plus morale at native x 106 (colsum.cpp:1171-1176). The wording of every label here is ours and lives in this file (decision 15); substitution is a replace and never str.format (decision 37), so a stray brace in a translated label cannot raise inside the render path and an unknown placeholder is left standing rather than swallowed.
output._deviation_note: DEVIATIONS, and (1) is smaller than it was. THE PRODUCTION ROWS NOW DRAW THE ORIGINAL'S OWN NET, not colony->production[t]. COLDRAW::Draw_Colony_Prod_Both_ (coldraw.cpp:36) computes what it draws before it draws anything, in four branches (coldraw.cpp:73-94), and only one of the four is production[t] itself; until 4 September 2026 this panel printed the stored value and called the difference a subset, which it is not - it is a different number. The four branches and the (int8_t) cast at coldraw.cpp:73 that chooses between them are transcribed in colonyrows.drawn_production. THE SHORTAGE IS DRAWN TOO, with the original's refusals mirrored - see _shortage_note. READING A NATIVE SCREENSHOT OF ONE OF THESE ROWS: THE GROUPS ARE SEPARATED BY AN EMPTY SLOT, NOT BY A GAP IN THE ARTWORK. Draw_Colony_Prod_Both_ advances drawn_count without drawing anything between groups - a bare drawn_count++ at coldraw.cpp:150 before the imports, and another at :147 after the secondary group - and it BUDGETS those slots into the width (total_units++ at coldraw.cpp:100 and :103). So a row reads left to right as net, gap, secondary, gap, imports, shortage. AND FOR NEGATIVE IMPORTS THE IMPORT GROUP USES THE NET'S OWN SPRITES: coldraw.cpp:152 sends that case to Prod_Anims_(prod_type, ...) at :154 and :158, the same artwork as the net at :118 and :123, so on screen the two groups are told apart ONLY by that empty slot. THIS IS HOW THE 4 SEPTEMBER 2026 REFERENCE SCREENSHOT WAS MISREAD: Wolf II's BC row - one gold bar and eight coins with an empty slot between them - was read as a single 18 and used to confirm a value that was 10 plus 8. Counting sprites across a gap is counting two numbers as one. WHAT IS STILL NOT DRAWN, and both are REACHABLE: imports[t] itself (coldraw.cpp:46, drawn with Import_Anims_ or Prod_Anims_ depending on the sign at coldraw.cpp:152), and the SECONDARY group - imports[ECON_INDUSTRY] on the FOOD row and pollution on the INDUSTRY row (coldraw.cpp:51-58). All three offsets are in the verified core/structs/colony.py - imports 243 i16[4], pollution 8 - so nothing is missing from the wire and this is not a data problem. They are not drawn because four numbers on one row of a 464x201 panel is a LAYOUT question, and opening it was not part of the package that fixed the net. Recorded rather than left to be noticed, the same form as the blockade in colonyrows.py: an omission nobody wrote down is indistinguishable from one nobody saw. (2) MORALE IS A NUMBER HERE AND A ROW OF ICONS THERE. COLDRAW::Draw_Info_Morale_Both_ draws abs(morale / 2) sprites, capped at 20, in one of two artworks depending on the sign. The sprites are in the player's LBX and are not shipped, which is the same reason the Buy control is a text button - see list._buy_note, where the same trade is made and marked. What IS transcribed is the value (the signed halving, C truncation toward zero) and the Unification rule below. A THIRD DEVIATION IS GONE, 3 September 2026: BC was not drawn, on the reading that the panel showed 'food, industry and research'. The original draws four. Its loop is `i < ECON_COUNT` and ECON_COUNT is 4 (orion2_consts.h:123), and the GEOMETRY settles it independently of the constant: y_pos starts at 349 and steps 18 (colsum.cpp:1170-1173), giving 349, 367, 385, 403, and morale is drawn at 421 (colsum.cpp:1176) - one step further on, which leaves room for exactly four rows above it and not three. The BC row is now drawn and the smoke check that asserted its absence is gone with it.
output._morale_note: UNDER UNIFICATION THE ORIGINAL DRAWS NO MORALE AT ALL. Draw_Info_Morale_Both_ sets its count to 0 when the owner's traits[TRAIT_CURRENT_GOVERNMENT] is GOVERNMENT_UNIFICATION or above (6 and 7, orion2_consts.h:199-200; the trait index is 0, orion2_consts.h:949). Transcribed: the row renders `hidden_value` rather than a zero, because a drawn 0 is a claim that morale is neutral and the original is claiming that morale does not apply. The trait comes from the verified s_player spec (traits @2308).
output._growth_note: The sum of s_colony.pop_growth[10] (offset 200), which is what colsum.cpp:1179-1182 accumulates into total_growth and passes to E_Strings_(74). THE k IS A UNIT, NOT A DECORATION. MOO2 counts population in thousands, so the number is thousands of colonists and the original prints it that way: its scan box read '+63k' on 3 September 2026, in the first --live --native side-by-side. The sign is explicit for the same reason the sidebar's Income and Food carry one - it is a net flow and a negative one means the colony is shrinking - and it comes from colonyempire.format_value, which is the one home for that rule. The 'k' is wording and lives here in the template (decision 15). WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: divide, round or scale. The engine's number is printed as the engine's number; only the unit that was always implied is now written down. Inventing a division to turn it into whole colonists would be reading a meaning into a field whose meaning still rests on the header's name alone. colsum.cpp:1180 also sums pop_roundoff[10] into total_roundoff and then never passes it to anything - not transcribed, because there is nothing to transcribe. The original colours a negative growth as well (colsum.cpp:1187-1190), which needs the inline attribute machinery and is not done here.
output._offsets_note: MEANING, NOT LAYOUT. s_colony and s_planet_data are verified specs, which fixes where every member sits and how wide it is and says nothing about what its values mean (decision 23). SIX OF THE SEVEN SCAN VALUES NOW AGREE WITH THE ORIGINAL'S OWN BOX. Read for Sadak I on 3 September 2026 in the second --live --native side-by-side, with both halves on the same sort key: the original printed 'Huge Desert / Normal Gravity / Mineral Rich / Population (4/8) / +63k' and this panel showed Huge, Desert, Normal, Rich, 4/8 and +63k. That closes growth, which had rested on the header's name alone; size, climate, gravity_class, mineral_class and n_pops had already been read against the original's planet description for Ixion II on 31 August, and max_pop is computed from them rather than read. MORALE IS THE ONE THAT DID NOT FALL, and the obstacle is an input capability and not the data. The comparison needs the original's box pointed at a colony with non-zero morale; _g_colony_n moves on HOVER (colsum.cpp:880-890), the Extension API cannot inject a hover, every click that lands on a row does something else instead, and the game's window is hidden while the API is on (platform.cpp:1379) so it cannot be hovered by hand. A save in which the colony the original is already scanning has non-zero morale settles it without any of that.
output._empty_note: EMPTY, and that is the point. With no colony selected the panel draws NOTHING - no labels, no dashes, no zeroes. The original's box is guarded by `_g_colony_n != -1` (colsum.cpp:1165) and simply is not drawn, and a zero would be a value where the original has an absence. Put a string here to have it drawn centred instead; a smoke check asserts the panel puts no ink on an empty selection while the shipped value is empty.
output._shortage_note: THE ORIGINAL DRAWS A SHORTAGE ON THESE ROWS AND THIS IS THE WORDING FOR IT (decision 15). COLDRAW::Draw_Colony_Prod_Both_ computes shortage = maintenance[t] - imports[t] - production[t], clamped to 0 at anything below 1 (coldraw.cpp:61-64), and draws it with COLONY::Short_Anims_ (coldraw.cpp:170-177) - the import sprite outlined in palette index 0xED (colony.cpp:2192-2199). We cannot resolve 0xED to an RGB value, because the palette is in the player's own LBX and is not shipped, so the marker is drawn in this screen's existing `warn` red, the one the sidebar reddens a negative Income with. RESOLVABLE SINCE core/lbx.py VIA THE SAME PALETTE (6 September 2026): COLSUM.LBX entry 0 carries all 256 indices and is the palette this screen sets - animate::Draw_Palette_(COLSUM::_anims[0]), colsum.cpp:128-129 - so 0xED has an RGB value a tool can read out of the player's own install. NOT APPLIED IN THIS PACKAGE, and the `warn` substitute stays: a colour read from a file that is not shipped cannot be the shipped default, and swapping it is its own decision with its own fallback to design. THE REFUSAL IS TRANSCRIBED TOO AND MATTERS MORE THAN THE SUM: those Short_Anims_ loops sit in the ELSE of `if (imports[t] < 0 || t == ECON_INDUSTRY)` (coldraw.cpp:152), so the original draws a shortage ONLY when imports are non-negative AND the row is not industry. A shortage on the industry row would be an invention wearing a citation - the number exists in the C++ and is never drawn there. See colonyrows.production_shortage. NO ELEMENT AT ALL WHEN THE SHORTAGE IS ZERO, not a 0 and not a dash: the original draws no sprite, and a zero would be a claim where it has an absence - the same rule as _empty_note and the Unification morale row. That decision is the NUMBER's and is taken in the renderer, so setting this template to something that renders '0' cannot bring the element back. Substitution is a replace, not str.format (decision 37). REFERENCE CASE, 4 September 2026: Wolf II, 13 pops, production[FOOD] 12, imports[FOOD] 0, maintenance[FOOD] 13 - so 13 - 0 - 12 = 1, and the original draws exactly one red marker on that row. POSITION: THE MARKER FOLLOWS THE VALUE, because that is the order the original draws in - net, gap, secondary, gap, imports, shortage, with the shortage LAST (coldraw.cpp:170-177, after the import loops). It sat to the LEFT until 4 September 2026, which inverted the only two groups this panel draws and also read badly: a leading '-2 10' takes the minus as a sign on the number after it, where '10 -2' reads as a value and an annotation. The pair is right-aligned AS A GROUP rather than hanging the marker past the value's right edge, for a measured reason: the widest structural marker (-255) is 19 to 41 px across the shipped sizes against a column_gap of 22 to 45, so it does not fit there, and the space beyond that gap is the panel's own margin where the frame's rim sits - the fault fixed in the sidebar the same day, see empire._text_inset_note. So the value shifts left on a row that has a marker, which is also closer to the original: its row is anchored at x and grows rightward rather than being pinned to a right edge. shortage_gap is the space between the two.
output._rows_note: ELEVEN VALUES, and the split follows the original's own two halves. LEFT is the scan paragraph: the seven values E_Strings_(74) carries - planet size, climate, gravity class, mineral class, n_pops, the computed maximum and growth (colsum.cpp:1198-1205) - in six rows, because the original prints n_pops and the maximum as one pair and so does this. RIGHT is the production column: all four ECON values (colsum.cpp:1171-1174 at native x 106, y 349 stepping 18) with morale under them (colsum.cpp:1176, y 421), which is the same order and the same grouping the original draws at native x 106. Morale is the eleventh row and is not one of the ten scan-and-production values: it is a count of sprites there, and a number here only because the sprites are not ours to ship. THREE OF THE SEVEN ARE ALSO IN THE ROW. climate, n_pops and max_pop are drawn per row as well (list._hd_extension), and that is not a duplication to clean up: the per-row line is the HD EXTENSION and THIS is the original's own box, which prints all seven for one colony. Removing them here would make the transcription a subset in order to tidy an extension.
output._geometry_note: TUNED AGAINST THE PICTURE, not against a rule. output_panel is 464 x 201 reference px and the fuller column holds six rows, so the pitch is (201 - 2*pad_y - 5*row_gap) / 6 and a column is (464 - 2*pad_x) / 2 = 216. column_gap 34 is the one number that came out of looking: at the first render it was 12, and 'Huge GROWTH' and 'Ultra Poor RESEARCH' read as single phrases because the left column's right-aligned value ended a few pixels from the right column's left-aligned label. Every number in that render was correct and the panel was unreadable, which is the failure mode the fundament's 'render it and look at it' rule exists for. Two smoke checks hold the result, both measured by rendering per decision 30. (a) The GUTTER between the columns must be at least one em of the value font - the rule the 34 was measured against and the one the 12 broke. (b) Within a column, each row's label must clear the widest value THAT ROW can show by at least one em of the label font. Per row, and that matters: pairing the widest label in the panel with the widest value in the panel asserts a collision that cannot happen, because POPULATION never prints 'Ultra Poor', and it failed at 1280x720 on exactly that imaginary pair. The real tightest is MINERALS against 'Ultra Poor', 21 px to spare at scale 1.0. Both at twelve resolutions.
output._info_note: THE LEFT PANEL IS THE ORIGINAL'S OWN DESCRIPTION BOX, and it is a TRANSCRIPTION. COLSUM::Draw_Colony_Scan_Info_ (colsum.cpp:1155) fills TWO boxes for the selected colony: BILL::Squeeze_Print_Formatted_Paragraph_(13, 354, 80, 88, buffer, 0) with seven values substituted into ESTRINGS::E_Strings_(74) (colsum.cpp:1194-1206), and the four production rows plus morale from native x 106 (colsum.cpp:1171-1176). planet_info is where the first belongs and planet_output where the second does; until 8 September 2026 both were drawn into planet_output and planet_info was empty. THE FORM IS SETTLED - 12 September 2026, Stage 5. It was provisional and info_style was the switch: 'paragraph' for E_Strings_(74)'s own five lines, 'rows' for the label-and-value table this panel drew before. Both were rendered beside the native, Data picked the paragraph, and the key is gone; render_info draws the transcription and nothing chooses. The `rows` renderer itself stays, because it is what planet_output draws. FIVE LINES AND NOT SIX ROWS: size and climate share a line, and growth carries no label at all. THE WORD-LIST RULE HOLDS FROM THE OTHER SIDE (see words._note): the lists hold the bare quality and the FORMAT supplies the noun, which is exactly what '%sravity' and 'Mineral %s' do in E_Strings_(74) - so the nouns are in info_paragraph here and never in the lists. The sixth argument 0 is JUSTIFY_LEFT, so the paragraph is left-aligned. AND THE WHOLE BOX REDDENS ON NEGATIVE GROWTH: the format takes the sign string twice, once before the first word and once before the number, and closes with an explicit reset, so the inline attribute spans the paragraph rather than the value - transcribed in colonyoutput.render_info.

header._deviation_window: DEVIATION - THE HEADER WINDOW IS OURS. The original has NO header window: it draws five raised plates straight onto the frame's metal, each a recessed dark field with a light rounded outline. Measured on the live framebuffer of screen 20 (reference save, 7 September 2026): plate interior luminance 44, surrounding metal 60, outline 96, and the plates SHARE their divider - two pixels at 85/93 between two interiors of 44, so the gap between plates is 0 and the divider is 6 reference px. We cut a header window and draw the plates inside it, so THE WINDOW'S OWN PANEL FILL STANDS IN FOR THE ORIGINAL'S PLATE RECESS: one dark field behind five outlines instead of five dark fields on metal. Chosen over closing the hole because with the header window removed the ring-to-list gap grows to about 74 reference px and the Stage A3 rail pass fills it with a stretched rail - buildable, but a change to the plate machinery plus a fill under every plate. DEVIATION - THE OUTLINE COLOUR: the original's line is a neutral grey at luminance 114-124; ours is panel.thin_border [55, 65, 85], luminance about 68 and blue, the project's own panel language (decision 34). The value lives in colors.json. AND THE PLATE HEIGHT IS A FINDING, NOT A CHOICE: the original's plate measures native y 11..32 = 22 px = 66 reference px, and the header window is 48 reference px of drawable height, so the transcribed plate is 37 % too tall to fit. The plates fill the window instead and colonyheader.PLATE_HEIGHT_REF records what they would be. Closing that gap means giving the header 66 px and taking 18 from the list (605 -> 587), which is a layout decision and not a drawing one.

build._note: THE BUILDING COLUMN'S WORDING (decision 15). The name itself is the ORIGINAL'S — COLBLDG::Selection_Name_ (colbldg.cpp:796) has THREE branches and core/prodname.py transcribes all three, two with a word and one with a stated absence. A BUILDING id (1..48) comes from the player's own TECHNAME.LBX via tools/techname_extract.py; an OPTION id comes from the player's own ESTRINGS.LBX via tools/estrings_extract.py, through the sixteen-case switch in COLBLDG::Option_String_ (colbldg.cpp:2338). Only these two lines are ours. THE REFERENCE SAVE TAKES THE OPTION BRANCH ON EVERY ROW: producing[0] is -2, COLONY_PRODUCTION_TRADE_GOODS, E_Strings_(0x21D) = 'Trade Goods'. That is why the column was empty until 7 September 2026 and why the fix was not a wider techname walk — the column was reading the wrong table for every row it had. || names_missing appears when a name file is absent or stale (a file an older extractor wrote), so the column says what is wrong instead of looking like a colony that builds nothing. The command that fixes it is in the log and in tools/setup.py's report, not here: a row 314 reference px wide cannot hold a path. || names_unsourced is a DIFFERENT state and needed its own words. A queued ship (id <= -100) is MOX::_ship[i].d.name and a ship design (-99..-50) is _player[owner].ship_designs[i].name; neither field is on the wire, core/structs/ship.py verifies five fields and a name at a guessed offset is what decision 23 forbids. NO EXTRACTION FIXES IT, so this wording must not name a command — sending a reader to run a tool that cannot help is worse than the blank it replaces. || AN EMPTY CELL IS OFTEN CORRECT AND IS NOT A STATE: E_Strings_(0x00C) is the empty string, and NONE, SEPARATOR and 0 all resolve to it (colbldg.cpp:2356-2359), so the original prints nothing there too. The column draws nothing and says nothing.
build._turns_note: THE '- 8t' SUFFIX IS NOT DRAWN AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. The original appends it from COLONY::Calculate_Current_Production_Turn_Count_ (colsum.cpp:588), a cost calculation over the colony's accumulated production and the item's price; neither the cost table nor the accumulation is established on the wire. producing_turns stays 0 and the suffix stays off, because a turn count nobody can source is a number a player would act on. OPEN, not approximated.
